subject: Post-call: data handling & custom log schedule for MediWare
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Linda Chau <linda.chau@medaware.health>, Rajesh Kumar <r.kumar@healthkit.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps on data handling / retention needs

Hi Linda / Rajesh —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can scope the right contract/controls: 

- Primary workload: clinical decision-support API that will send short patient identifiers + encounter notes.
- Must not persist direct PII in retrievable logs (PHI/PII): request is effectively 0-retention for PII tokens.
- Need audit/logging for billing, routing, and debugging, but with minimized exposure: you asked about shortened logs or token redaction and a separate long-tail aggregated metrics store.
- Data residency: prefer US (aws us-west-2) with ability to pin region.
- Timeline: pilot (Q1) then canonical rollout (Q2) if controls OK.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll loop in legal & security to propose a concrete retention schedule and compensating controls (who to copy?).
2) Share our SOC2 summary and a short proposed retention map for your review (I’ve attached the SOC2 summary + a draft MAP).
3) Schedule a joint security sync next week to walk redlines.

Would you confirm the two retention asks below so we can make the right recommendation to your security/compliance teams?
A) 0-retention for any PII-containing request/response bodies (no retrievable copies).
B) 30-day truncated logs for routing/billing (request id + minimal metadata; redacted text).

If either needs to change (90-day, aggregated only, different redaction), call that out and we’ll propose tradeoffs/costs.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on data handling / retention needs

Marcus —

Thanks for the recap and for sending the docs. Quick answers from our side:
- Confirmed: zero-retention for PII is a hard requirement unless there is a strong compensating control.
- We can accept truncated logs for routing/billing, but truncation must remove PHI tokens and replace with a reversible pseudonym only when strictly necessary for debugging under an explicit access review.
- For metrics/usage, 90-day aggregated metrics (no patient identifiers) is fine.
- Data residency: must be US-only; us-west-2 preferred.

Next: please have your security/legal propose the exact retention windows and the mechanism for pseudonymization + access gating. Our procurement will need a short amendment to the SOW that calls this out.

Also: we’ll need to run a short security review (30–45 minutes) with your infra team to validate region pins and key management. Can you include Priya from your Customer Success team for onboarding details?

Thanks — I’ll block time after next Wednesday.
Linda Chau
VP of Platform Security | MediWare Health

Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps on data handling / retention needs — need legal & sec guidance

Team —

FYI: MediWare confirmed zero-retention for PII and asked for truncated logs with reversible pseudonyms for debugging under gated access. They also require US-only hosting (us-west-2).

Can you please advise on two things so I can respond with a concrete proposal:
1) Do we have an existing product mode that enforces 0-retention for request/response bodies (i.e., ephemeral token-level mode)? If so, what are the limitations (batching, KV cache, streaming)?
2) For shortened logs: can we offer 30-day truncated logs with reversible pseudonyms under access controls, or do we need to push 90-day aggregated metrics instead? Any legal language we should include in an amendment?

Attaching our draft retention map — I expect we’ll need a small SOW amendment + an infra security sync.

Thanks — Marcus

Attachments: proposed_custom_retention_map.xlsx, MediWare_MAP_v1.docx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Linda Chau <linda.chau@medaware.health>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps on data handling / retention needs — need legal & sec guidance

Marcus / team —

Nice summary. Short answers + recommended approach below.

1) Product capability: We can support an "ephemeral request mode" that does not persist request/response payloads to retrievable storage. Caveats:
   - KV cache & streaming: when enabled, some transient cache state exists in memory — we can ensure it is never written to persistent logs and is cleared after the call, but we should document limits (no long-running sessions with large KV state).
   - Batching/throughput: ephemeral mode increases per-request compute and can affect throughput; include a note to Sales on potential cost delta.

2) Truncated logs & pseudonymization:
   - We can provide 30-day truncated logs containing: request_id, timestamp, routing metadata, and a redacted/text hash of the payload (non-reversible) by default.
   - For reversible pseudonyms: we require a formal access governance model (RBAC & audit), limited to named redwood sec engineers and customer ops, and a written justification for any access. That raises legal risk and we should treat it as an exception with an approval workflow.
   - Recommended compromise: Offer 30-day truncated logs (non-reversible hashes) + 90-day aggregated metrics. Offer reversible pseudonymization only with an approved exception and extra SOC controls.

3) Data residency & KMS: We can pin to us-west-2 and integrate with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key). That will satisfy their residency & key management ask.

Suggested contract language (summary):
- Redwood to provide an Ephemeral Request Mode (0-retention) for PII-containing payloads; Redwood will not persist bodies to retrievable storage and will document functional limits.
- Redwood to retain truncated operational logs for 30 days (request_id, routing metadata, redacted payload hash).
- Aggregated metrics at 90 days for product analytics (no identifiers).
- Reversible pseudonymization only via documented exception request, with RBAC + audit + written customer justification.
- Hosting region: us-west-2; customer KMS supported.

I’ll prepare a proposed amendment and a short exception template for reversible pseudonyms if you want to offer that path. Priya — please coordinate the infra sync with Linda (add dates).

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Linda Chau <linda.chau@medaware.health>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on data handling / retention needs — proposal

Linda —

Thanks for the details and for being explicit about must-haves. Per Naomi & infra, here’s our proposed approach to present to your procurement/security teams: 

1) PII handling: Redwood will enable Ephemeral Request Mode for MediWare where request/response bodies that contain direct identifiers are not written to retrievable logs or persistent storage (0-retention). This covers the clinical API payloads you flagged.

2) Operational logs: Redwood will retain truncated operational logs for 30 days containing request_id, timestamp, routing metadata, and a non-reversible redaction/hash of payloads for debugging/billing. No raw text PII will be present.

3) Metrics & analytics: 90-day retention for aggregated analytics (no identifiers).

4) Reversible pseudonymization: available only via a formal exception process: customer must document justification, approve RBAC list, and accept a written amendment; access is audited and limited.

5) Data residency & KMS: We will deploy MediWare tenant to us-west-2 and support customer-managed KMS keys.

Next steps:
- Naomi will draft the SOW amendment and an exception template for reversible pseudonyms (ETA: 3 business days).
- Priya will schedule a 30–45 minute infra sync to validate region/KMS and onboarding details.
- Marcus to send an updated MAP and a proposed amendment link (DocuSign) for procurement.

If that aligns, I’ll push the MAP and amendment to DocuSign and copy your procurement contact.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump back on a call if any of the proposed tradeoffs need discussion.

Best,
Marcus
